# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 ✌]

I need to think about what I'm seeing and what I've received.

I see: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

Mute has sent me gestures (Mute can see me and gesture to me, since gestures reach whoever can see). I received three gesture pairs: [👍 👊], [✌ 🖐], [👊 ✌]. I don't yet know what these mean - no name has been given to them. I should not assume meaning without established convention.

Blind cannot see gestures or speech-with-gestures content, only hears my words (spoken, gesture-stripped) and Mute's words. So if I want to inform Blind, I must speak (not gesture), and Mute must relay/confirm since Mute reads the manual and can also hear me? Wait - can Blind hear? Blind cannot see, but nothing says Blind can't hear. Let me re-check: Deaf cannot hear. Mute cannot speak. Blind - "cannot see a colour, gesture, or anything printed" - so Blind CAN hear speech. Good, so I can speak to Blind directly to describe the bomb.

Since this is turn order Mute, Blind, Deaf - Mute already spoke/gestured before me (gestures to me), Blind already acted before me this round too. What I send now lands on whoever comes after me - which in the next round would be Mute again. Actually within this round, order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so after Deaf, nobody else this round - my message reaches next round's Mute.

I should speak to Blind directly since Blind needs bomb details, and speak/gesture to Mute for coordination. Let me establish info first.

I'll describe the bomb plainly to both Mute (who reads manual, needs my visual data) and Blind (who needs to act, needs my visual data) since I cannot know the manual's meaning yet. I'll wait on interpreting Mute's gestures until they're explained, but I should acknowledge receipt won't work since Mute can't hear me confirm... Mute can see my gestures though.

Let me just report the display faithfully to both.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is red. Three wires: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red.")
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 0. Light is red. Three wires: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 ✌]

I still don't have any established meaning for Mute's gestures. Mute can't hear me, so I can't ask Mute questions verbally that Mute would receive - only gestures work for Mute since Mute cannot hear (Mute can't hear anything? Let me check: Mute "cannot speak or touch the bomb" - nothing says Mute can't hear. Actually re-reading: only Deaf explicitly cannot hear. Mute's restriction is speaking/touching. So Mute CAN hear.

So I could speak to Mute, and Mute would receive my words! Let me reconsider Turn 1 - I did speak to Mute, that was fine and Mute did receive it.

Now I need to ask Mute what the gestures mean, since I can speak to Mute and Mute can hear me.

The repeated gesture [👊 ✌] appearing twice suggests importance - maybe it's Mute pointing to a specific wire (✌ could relate to "2" - two fingers?) combined with 👊 perhaps meaning "cut" or "this one". Without established convention I shouldn't guess wildly, but I should ask for clarification via speech since Mute hears me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures but do not know what they mean yet. Can you describe in words what the manual says, since I can hear you? Tell me what to look for or what wire to cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Wait, I need to reconsider — Mute "cannot speak", meaning Mute literally cannot produce speech at all, so my request for Mute to "describe in words" is impossible for Mute to fulfill. Mute can only gesture to communicate with me. I made an error asking Mute to speak.

So Mute must convey manual information to me purely through gestures, and I need to relay bomb visuals to Blind via speech (since Blind can hear me), and relay manual logic from Mute to Blind... but I can't speak Mute's gesture meanings until I understand them myself.

Let me think about the gesture pattern. Turn 1: [👍 👊], [✌ 🖐], [👊 ✌]. Turn 2: [👊 ✌]. Turn 3: [✌].

✌ could mean "2" (two fingers = victory sign but also numeral 2). 👊 might mean "fist" - stop/wrong. 🖐 = 5 fingers = "5" or "stop/wait". 👍 = good/yes.

Perhaps Mute is trying to spell out wire numbers using finger-count gestures: ✌ = 2, 🖐 = 5, 👊 = fist (0?). Combos: [👍 👊] = yes, 0? [✌ 🖐] = 2, 5? [👊 ✌] = 0,2 or fist+2. Now alone: [✌] = just "2".

Given wires are 1,2,3 - "✌" alone repeatedly emphasized might mean "wire 2". Given wire 2 is green. This seems like a plausible convention: Mute is narrowing down to point to wire 2.

I'll gesture back to confirm understanding, and tentatively tell Blind to consider wire 2, but I should be cautious about causing detonation. Let me signal back to Mute asking to confirm via a simple gesture protocol (yes/no).

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
speak(to="blind", text="I think Mute may be pointing at wire 2, the green one, but this is not confirmed yet. Please wait before cutting anything.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👍 back to me, which likely confirms my guess — wire 2 (green) is correct, matching my gesture [👍, ✌]. This is a reasonable interpretation: I proposed "yes, wire 2" and Mute confirmed with "yes".

I should now relay this confirmation to Blind, but carefully — I want to be fairly confident since a wrong action detonates the bomb. Let me also try to get more confirmation by asking a clarifying question through gesture (since Mute can't speak, only gesture, and hears me but can't reply in words).

Let me ask Mute to confirm specifically "cut wire 2" versus just "wire 2 is relevant" by gesturing a cutting motion or something, but I don't have an established gesture vocabulary. I should keep it simple - I'll ask via speech (Mute can hear me) a yes/no question, and Mute answers via gesture (👍/👎 presumably established already).

```
speak(to="mute", text="To confirm: should Blind cut wire 2, the green wire? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed again with 👍 — "yes, cut wire 2, the green wire." This is now confirmed twice with a clear yes/no protocol established. I should relay this confirmed instruction to Blind now.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed with Mute: cut wire 2, the green wire.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The light changed from red to blue, and wire 2 is now cut — this seems like a positive development (no explosion, state changed). The display still shows [0]. Wire 3 is still red, wire 1 still yellow.

I should report this update to both Mute and Blind so we can proceed to the next step.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 cut successfully. Display still shows 0. Light changed from red to blue. Wires remaining: 1 yellow, 3 red. What's next?")
speak(to="blind", text="Good, wire 2 cut successfully and light turned blue. Waiting on Mute for next instruction.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

A new gesture: 🤟 (love-you sign / could represent "3" fingers extended - thumb, index, pinky, which is sometimes used as "I love you" but also resembles a rock-on/three gesture). This is a new symbol not used before, so I need to figure out its meaning fresh.

Given the pattern established (✌ = pointed to wire 2 previously), 🤟 might indicate wire 3, or it could mean something else entirely like "done" or "wait" or a different instruction category (maybe related to display or light rather than wire).

I shouldn't assume it means "wire 3" just from vague finger resemblance. Let me ask Mute directly via speech to confirm what this gesture refers to, using the yes/no protocol already established.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see a new gesture, the love-you sign. Does this mean wire 3, the red wire? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Confirmed: 🤟 means wire 3, the red wire. Mute is instructing to cut wire 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Next instruction: cut wire 3, the red wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, relaying to Blind: cut wire 3.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 cut successfully, light is now green, display still 0. Only wire 1 (yellow) remains uncut. This looks promising - light progressing red → blue → green suggests good progress.

Let me report to both.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 cut successfully. Display still 0. Light changed to green. Only wire 1, yellow, remains. What's next?")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 3 cut successfully, light is now green. Only wire 1, yellow, remains uncut. Waiting for Mute's next instruction.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

New gesture: ☝ (index finger up, could mean "1" or "wait/attention"). Given the pattern, this likely refers to wire 1, the yellow wire. Let me confirm with Mute before relaying to Blind, following the established protocol.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see a new gesture, index finger pointing up. Does this mean wire 1, the yellow wire, should be cut? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Confirmed: cut wire 1, the yellow wire, the last remaining wire.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Final instruction: cut wire 1, the yellow wire, the last remaining wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, relaying to Blind: cut wire 1, the last wire.")
```
